title: Which material makes the best umbrella?

explain.say: It is rainy season in Lagos, and you need an umbrella. But what if it were made of paper? Splosh! Let's test some materials, like real scientists, to find out which ones keep the rain out.

draw.text: Which material makes the best umbrella?

explain.say: See the Waterproof group lighting up? Waterproof means water cannot get through. Drops of water sit on top of a plastic bag, rubber, foil or waxed cloth, and roll off. Which of these could make an umbrella?

Now Soaks it up glows. Paper, cotton, kitchen towel and wool are absorbent, which means they soak up water like a sponge. Kitchen towel is great for spills, but a terrible umbrella! Can you think of something absorbent in your bathroom?

To be sure, you need a fair test, which means changing only one thing: the material. See the first step lighting up? Cut every piece the same size. Then use the same number of drops and wait the same time for each. Why do you think everything else must stay the same?

steps.label: Same size pieces
steps.note: Cut every material the same size.

steps.label: Check underneath
steps.note: Is the paper below wet or dry?

explain.say: Last step: check underneath! If the paper below stays dry, the material is waterproof. Excellent testing, scientist! Wow fact: lotus leaves are so waterproof that raindrops roll off them like marbles, washing away dirt as they go.

steps.label: Same size pieces
steps.note: Cut every material the same size.

steps.label: Check underneath
steps.note: Is the paper below wet or dry?

faq.a: Plastic, rubber, metal foil, glass and waxed or coated cloth are waterproof: water cannot pass through them.
Absorbent means a material soaks up water into tiny gaps inside it, like a sponge. Paper, cotton, towels and wool are absorbent.
asks: Why do towels soak up water?

faq.a: A fair test is an experiment where you change only one thing and keep everything else the same, so you know what caused the result.
asks: How do you make a test fair?

faq.q: Why is an umbrella not made of paper?
faq.a: Paper is absorbent: it soaks up rain, goes soggy and tears. An umbrella needs a waterproof, light and strong material like coated nylon.
asks: Can you make a paper umbrella?

faq.q: Why do raindrops roll off some leaves?
faq.a: Some leaves, like lotus leaves, have a waxy, bumpy surface that water cannot stick to, so the drops stay round and roll off. This is called the lotus effect.

facts: Lotus leaves are super water-repellent because of microscopic bumps covered in wax, which make water roll off (the lotus effect).
In a fair test only one variable is changed while the others are kept the same.

quiz.say: Which material would make the best umbrella?
quiz.why: Plastic is waterproof, so rain runs off it.

wrong.0: Kitchen towel is absorbent and would soak up the rain.
wrong.2: Cotton wool soaks up water and falls apart.

quiz.say: Zara tests materials but uses 10 drops on some and 30 drops on others. What is wrong?
quiz.show: What is wrong with Zara's test?

options.show: It is not a fair test
options.say: It is not a fair test

quiz.why: The amount of water must be the same for every material for the test to be fair.

wrong.0: Changing the drops as well as the material makes the result unclear.
wrong.2: The amount is fine; the problem is that it is not the same each time.
